questions.title: If you hit your first shot from the wrong place
questions.question: You hit your ball for the first shot, but your feet were not in the right tee area. What should you do so you can keep playing the hole?

choices.text: Go find your ball and keep playing as normal. No penalty.
Hit your first shot again from inside the tee area and add two extra shots to your score.
Hit your shot again from anywhere you want, and just get a warning.
Ask the person you are playing with if you can keep going from where your ball is.

questions.explanation: You must play your first shot again from the right spot—the tee area. You need to add two extra shots to your score for that hole.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The place where you start the hole. It is between two markers and behind the line made by them.
An extra shot added to your score because of a mistake.

questions.teachingTip: Draw the tee area on the ground with cones or ropes and let children practise placing their ball and feet correctly before swinging.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids might think they can keep playing if no one saw the mistake.
Some might believe they only need to move their ball if it is outside the tee area, not their feet.

questions.title: Correcting a teeing area mistake
questions.question: After realising you hit your tee shot from outside the teeing area in stroke play, what should you do to avoid being disqualified?

choices.text: Go to your ball and continue playing, no penalty.
Replay your shot from within the teeing area and add two penalty strokes.
Replay from anywhere you like with just a warning.
Ask your opponent for permission to keep playing from where you are.

questions.explanation: You must replay your shot from within the teeing area and take two penalty strokes to avoid disqualification.
